=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:17-18 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The consumer template's `workflow_run` trigger omits the required `workflows` key.
  WHY: actionlint rejects the trigger, leaving the required CI check red and blocking the PR; `workflows: ["*"]` is needed to listen to every workflow.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:118 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The test asserts that the consumer trigger equals `{"types": ["completed"]}`, pinning the missing `workflows` key.
  WHY: After the template includes `workflows: ["*"]`, this exact-equality assertion fails.
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:105-172 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: After `do_POST` partially reads a request body, `_reject()` resets its drain count to the full `Content-Length` instead of the unread remainder.
  WHY: The drain can wait up to the one-second deadline for bytes already consumed; severity is high per reviewers rating it MAJOR, while other reviewers rate it NIT and note the deadline bounds the wait and HTTP 400 is still returned.
- README.md:1216-1221 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The README says the consumer wrapper omits the workflow-name filter, which disagrees with the required `workflows: ["*"]` configuration.
  WHY: Operators will be misled about how the trigger matches all workflows; severity is high per reviewers rating it MAJOR, while google_gemini-3_8-flash rates it NIT.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:37-44 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The reusable workflow makes `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN` a required `workflow_call` secret, which breaks startup for consumers that have not configured it.
  WHY: Those consumers' triage runs fail during pre-job setup with “Required secret is not provided” until they add the token.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Consumers listen to `"*"` and skip the pipeline's own `AI …` workflows" (PR Description, "Which workflows (Q55)")
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml `on.workflow_run` block
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml omits the `workflows` keyword; tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:118 asserts the trigger has no `workflows` key; README.md:1216-1221 describes omission; actionlint reports “no workflow is configured for 'workflow_run' event”.
- requirement: “Operators see no skipped wrapper run for every finished workflow in consumer repos.”
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml `on.workflow_run` block, plus the predicate comment in `workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:14-18`
  confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The PR description acknowledges this noise as “an explicitly documented operational tradeoff required by Q55”; the predicate lives inside the job `if:`, so every workflow run, including `AI …` workflows, wakes the workflow and only the job short-circuits.
- requirement: The relay's `_reject` drain should bound its wait by the unread body, not the full Content-Length, when called from a partial-read rejection path.
  expected_change_site: scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:110 (`body_remaining = int(length)` inside `_reject`)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: After `do_POST` partially reads, `_reject` re-initializes `body_remaining` from the full `Content-Length` rather than `int(length) - bytes_already_consumed`; the drain can spend up to the 1 s socket-timeout window waiting for bytes already consumed.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:17-18 (workflow_run trigger) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The consumer template's `workflow_run` event declaration omits the required `workflows` key.
  WHY: actionlint rejects it, causing the required CI / lint check to fail and blocking the PR; consumer repos would receive the rejected template on the next `@stable` sync.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:118 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts `_on(data)["workflow_run"] == {"types": ["completed"]}`, locking in the consumer template without `workflows`.
  WHY: After adding `workflows: ["*"]` to the template, the parsed YAML includes that key and the assertion fails.
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:105-123 (_reject drain) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: After `do_POST` partially reads the body, `_reject` initializes `body_remaining` from the full Content-Length despite the read position having advanced.
  WHY: The drain terminates on empty-read or the one-second deadline, so there is no runtime crash; the counter mismatch is a minor logic-clarity issue.
- README.md:1219-1221 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The README says “the consumer wrapper omits the workflow-name filter to listen to every workflow”.
  WHY: After adding `workflows: ["*"]`, that wording describes a different mechanism than the implementation.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml:lines 17-18 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `workflow_run` trigger configuration omits the required `workflows` field.
  WHY: actionlint reports “no workflow is configured for 'workflow_run' event”, causing the required CI / lint check to fail.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:line 118 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts that the consumer wrapper's `workflow_run` mapping equals `{"types": ["completed"]}`, pinning the omission of the `workflows` key.
  WHY: Once the template includes `workflows: ["*"]`, the assertion fails.
- README.md:lines 1219-1221 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Documentation says the consumer wrapper omits the workflow-name filter to listen to every workflow.
  WHY: When `workflows: ["*"]` is restored to resolve actionlint, the documentation contradicts the workflow configuration.
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py:lines 170-172 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When `do_POST` has an incomplete or timed-out body read, `_reject()` attempts to drain the full Content-Length again.
  WHY: Since part of the payload was already read, `_reject()` can wait until the one-second socket deadline before returning HTTP 400.

  PROBLEM: The consumer template's `workflow_run` trigger omits the `workflows` key; actionlint rejects the trigger and the intended match-all behavior requires `workflows: ["*"]`.
  WHY: The required CI / lint check fails on every push, so the PR is blocked and the triage workflow does not ship to consumer repos.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py:line 118, `assert _on(data)["workflow_run"] == {"types": ["completed"]}` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test pins the broken state by asserting that the consumer trigger has no `workflows` key.
  WHY: Adding `workflows: ["*"]` makes the test fail.
- README.md:lines 1216-1221, "the consumer wrapper omits the workflow-name filter to listen to every workflow and skips the pipeline's own `AI …` workflows" | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The README says the consumer template omits the `workflows` filter, but actionlint requires `workflows: ["*"]`.
  WHY: The documentation would describe a different implementation and could lead consumer maintainers to copy the rejected omission.
- scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py: `_reject` method (lines 102-131), `body_remaining = int(length)` inside the drain block | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After `do_POST` partially reads the body, `_reject` reinitializes `body_remaining` from the full Content-Length rather than the actual remaining bytes.
  WHY: The drain can spend up to the one-second socket-timeout window waiting for bytes that were already consumed.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:lines 37-44, `secrets: { GH_PAT, CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, TG_BOT_SECRET, ... required: true }` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The reusable workflow adds `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN: required: true` to its `workflow_call` secret contract, breaking startup for consumers that have not configured the secret.
  WHY: Consumer triage runs fail during pre-job setup with “Required secret is not provided” until the operator adds the fine-grained PAT.
